canonical.title: Recover Binary Search Tree (Two Swapped Nodes)
canonical.sourceFilePath: 12. Binary Search Trees/2. Practice Problems/11. Recover BST.cpp

narrative.title: The Two Misfiled Bins Swap-Back
narrative.scenario: Overnight, exactly two bins in a size-sorted storage tree were swapped by a forklift mix-up. The floor plan is intact — only the size labels on those two bins are wrong. A checker walks the shelves in sorted order, flags the first and last spots where the rising sequence dips, and re-prints those two labels to restore perfect order without touching a single shelf.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) in which exactly two node values have been swapped.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the repaired tree serialized as a level-order array with trailing nulls trimmed — structure unchanged, the two swapped values restored.
constraints: Exactly two values are out of place; a solution exists
Follow-up: O(1) extra space is possible with Morris traversal

testCases.explanation: The inorder walk 3, 1, 2 dips once; swapping 3 and 1 restores the BST.
The walk 1, 3, 2, 4 dips at 3→2; swapping 3 and 2 repairs the order.

hintLevels: Level 1: Read the tree in sorted order; a broken BST shows up as dips in that reading.
Level 2: Track the previous visited node — record 'first' at the first dip and keep updating 'last' at every later dip.
Level 3: Adjacent swaps produce one dip, far-apart swaps two — swapping first.previous with last fixes both patterns.
